translations.literal: Biographies 64: Literary Arts (Part Two) — Zhao Feng, Zhou Ang, Wang Tingyun, Liu Ang, Li Jing, Liu Congyi, Lü Zhongfu and Zhang Jian, Li Chunfu, Wang Yu, Song Jiujia, Pang Zhu, Li Xianneng, Wang Ruoxu, Wang Yuanjie, Sun Guogang, Ma Jiuchou, Li Fen, son of Yuan Deming: Yuan Haowen
translations.idiomatic: Biography 64, Continuation of Literary Arts — Zhao Feng, Zhou Ang, Wang Tingyun, Liu Ang, Li Jing, Liu Congyi, Lü Zhongfu and Zhang Jian, Li Chunfu, Wang Yu, Song Jiujia, Pang Zhu, Li Xianneng, Wang Ruoxu, Wang Yuanjie, Sun Guogang, Ma Jiuchou, Li Fen, and Yuan Haowen, son of Yuan Deming

sentences.zh: 趙渢，字文孺，東平人。

translations.literal: Zhao Feng, styled Wenru, was a man of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Feng, whose style name was Wenru, came from Dongping.

sentences.zh: 大定二十二年進士，仕至禮部郎中。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the twenty-second year of Dading; he served to Director of Rituals in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-second year of the Dading reign and rose to Director of Rituals in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 性沖淡，學道有所得。

translations.literal: His nature was calm and detached; in studying the Way he gained real attainment.
translations.idiomatic: By temperament he was serene and unworldly, and in his pursuit of the Way he achieved genuine insight.

sentences.zh: 尤工書，自號「黃山」。

translations.literal: He was especially skilled at calligraphy and styled himself "Mount Huang."
translations.idiomatic: He excelled above all in calligraphy and took the sobriquet "Mount Huang."

sentences.zh: 趙秉文雲：「渢之正書體兼顏、蘇，行草備諸家體，其超放又似楊凝式，當處蘇、黃伯仲間。

translations.literal: Zhao Bingwen said: "In regular script Feng's manner combines Yan and Su; in running and cursive script he commands every school's style; his bold freedom also resembles Yang Ningshi — he should stand between Su and Huang as their peer."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Bingwen remarked: "In regular script, Feng's hand blends Yan Zhenqing and Su Shi; in running and cursive script he has mastered every major school. His bold, unfettered manner also recalls Yang Ningshi — he belongs in the same rank as Su and Huang."

sentences.zh: 」党懷英小篆，李陽冰以來鮮有及者，時人以渢配之，號曰「党趙」。

translations.literal: In small seal script Dang Huaiying had scarcely been matched since Li Yangbing; contemporaries paired Feng with him, calling them "Dang and Zhao."
translations.idiomatic: Dang Huaiying's small seal script had scarcely been equaled since Li Yangbing's day, and people of the time paired Feng with him, dubbing the two "Dang and Zhao."

sentences.zh: 有《黃山集》行於世。

translations.literal: His Collected Works of Mount Huang circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His Collected Works of Mount Huang circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 周昂，字德卿，真定人。

translations.literal: Zhou Ang, styled Deqing, was a man of Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Ang, whose style name was Deqing, came from Zhending.

sentences.zh: 父伯祿字天錫，大定進士，仕至同知沁南軍節度使。

translations.literal: His father Bo Lu, styled Tiansi, was a jinshi in the Dading era and served to Vice Commissioner of the Qinnan Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: His father Bo Lu, styled Tiansi, had passed the jinshi examination in the Dading reign and rose to Vice Commissioner of the Qinnan Military Commission.

sentences.zh: 昂年二十四擢第。

translations.literal: Ang passed the examination at age twenty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Ang won his degree at the age of twenty-four.

sentences.zh: 調南和簿，有異政。

translations.literal: He was assigned as registrar of Nanhe and achieved outstanding administration.
translations.idiomatic: Posted as registrar of Nanhe, he distinguished himself with exceptional governance.

sentences.zh: 遷良鄉令，入拜監察御史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to magistrate of Liangxiang, then entered court as Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to magistrate of Liangxiang and later summoned to serve as Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 路鐸以言事被斥，昂送以詩，語涉謗訕，坐停銓。

translations.literal: When Lu Duo was dismissed for remonstrance, Ang sent him a poem whose language touched on slander; for this Ang was barred from appointment.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Duo was dismissed for speaking out on policy, Ang sent him a parting poem whose wording bordered on defamation, and Ang was consequently barred from further appointments.

sentences.zh: 久之，起為隆州都軍，以邊功複召為三司官。

translations.literal: After a long while he was reappointed Commander of Long Prefecture; for frontier merit he was again summoned as an official of the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was reappointed military commander of Long Prefecture, and for his achievements on the frontier he was summoned back as an official of the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 大安兵興，權行六部員外郎。

translations.literal: When war arose in the Da'an era, he served provisionally as Vice Director in the Six Ministries.
translations.idiomatic: When hostilities broke out in the Da'an era, he served provisionally as Vice Director in the Six Ministries.

sentences.zh: 其甥王若虛嘗學於昂，昂教之曰：「文章工於外而拙於內者，可以驚四筵而不可以適獨坐，可以取口稱而不可以得首肯。

translations.literal: His nephew Wang Ruoxu once studied under Ang. Ang taught him: "Writings skilled outwardly yet clumsy inwardly may startle a hall of four tables yet cannot satisfy solitary reading; they may win spoken praise yet cannot earn a nod of assent."
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Wang Ruoxu had once studied under him. Ang instructed him: "Prose that is polished on the surface but hollow within may dazzle a banquet hall yet fail to hold up in quiet reading; it may win applause yet never earn a true nod of agreement."

sentences.zh: 」又雲：「文章以意為主，以言語為役，主強而役弱則無令不從。

translations.literal: He also said: "In writing, meaning is master and language is servant; when the master is strong and the servant weak, no command goes unheeded."
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "In writing, the idea must be master and language the servant; when the master is strong and the servant subordinate, every command is obeyed."

sentences.zh: 今人往往驕其所役，至跋扈難制，甚者反役其主，雖極辭語之工，而豈文之正哉。」

translations.literal: People today often make their servants arrogant until they become overbearing and hard to control; in extreme cases the servant rules the master. However polished the diction, how can that be proper writing?"
translations.idiomatic: Writers today often let language grow arrogant until it becomes unruly and ungovernable; in the worst cases language enslaves the idea. However exquisite the phrasing, how can that be genuine prose?"

sentences.zh: 昂孝友，喜名節，學術醇正，文筆高雅，諸儒皆師尊之。

translations.literal: Ang was filial and friendly, cherished integrity and reputation, his learning pure and correct, his prose lofty and refined; all scholars honored him as their teacher.
translations.idiomatic: Ang was devoted to family and friends, prized integrity and reputation, pursued learning of rare purity, and wrote in an elevated style; scholars everywhere regarded him as a master.

sentences.zh: 既曆台省，為人所擠，竟坐詩得罪，謫東海上十數年。

translations.literal: After serving in the censorate and secretariat he was squeezed out by others and in the end offended through a poem; he was banished to the eastern sea for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: After serving in the censorate and secretariat he was pushed aside by rivals and ultimately fell afoul of the authorities over a poem, spending more than a decade in exile on the eastern coast.

sentences.zh: 始入翰林，言事愈切。

translations.literal: When he first entered the Hanlin Academy his remonstrances grew ever sharper.
translations.idiomatic: When he first entered the Hanlin Academy, his memorials on policy grew ever more forthright.

sentences.zh: 出佐三司非所好，從宗室承裕軍。

translations.literal: Serving as aide in the Three Departments was not to his liking; he followed the imperial clansman Chengyu's army.
translations.idiomatic: A post assisting the Three Departments did not suit him, so he joined the army of the imperial clansman Chengyu.

sentences.zh: 承裕失利，跳走上穀，眾欲徑歸，昂獨不從，城陷，與其從子嗣明同死於難。

translations.literal: When Chengyu suffered defeat and fled to Shanggu, the troops wished to return directly; Ang alone would not follow. When the city fell, he and his nephew Siming died together in the calamity.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengyu was defeated and fled toward Shanggu, the troops wanted to march straight home, but Ang alone refused. When the city fell, he and his nephew Siming perished together in the disaster.

sentences.zh: 嗣明字晦之。

translations.literal: Siming was styled Huizhi.
translations.idiomatic: Siming's style name was Huizhi.

sentences.zh: 王庭筠

translations.literal: Wang Tingyun
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tingyun

sentences.zh: 王庭筠，字子端，遼東人。

translations.literal: Wang Tingyun, styled Ziduan, was a man of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tingyun, whose style name was Ziduan, came from Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 生未期，視書識十七字。

translations.literal: Before he was a hundred days old, upon seeing a book he recognized seventeen characters.
translations.idiomatic: Before he was even a hundred days old, he could recognize seventeen characters at a glance in a book.

sentences.zh: 七歲學詩，十一歲賦全題。

translations.literal: At seven he studied poetry; at eleven he composed on a full examination topic.
translations.idiomatic: At seven he began studying poetry, and at eleven he could compose a complete examination essay on an assigned theme.

sentences.zh: 稍長，涿郡王翛一見，期以國士。

translations.literal: When he grew somewhat older, Wang Xiao of Zhuo Commandery met him once and marked him as a national talent.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew older, Wang Xiao of Zhuo Commandery met him once and pronounced him a man of national stature.

sentences.zh: 登大定十六年進士第。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the sixteenth year of Dading.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the sixteenth year of the Dading reign.

sentences.zh: 調恩州軍事判官，臨政即有聲。

translations.literal: He was assigned as military adjutant of En Prefecture and at once gained renown in office.
translations.idiomatic: Posted as military adjutant of En Prefecture, he quickly earned a reputation for effective governance.

sentences.zh: 郡民鄒四者謀為不軌，事覺，逮捕千餘人，而鄒四竄匿不能得。

translations.literal: A townsman named Zou Si plotted sedition; when the affair was exposed more than a thousand were arrested, yet Zou Si fled into hiding and could not be seized.
translations.idiomatic: A local man named Zou Si plotted rebellion. When the plot was uncovered, more than a thousand people were arrested, but Zou Si escaped into hiding and could not be captured.

sentences.zh: 朝廷遣大理司直王仲軻治其獄，庭筠以計獲鄒四，分別詿誤，坐預謀者十二人而已。

translations.literal: The court sent Wang Zhongke, Direct Investigator of the Court of Judicial Review, to handle the case. Tingyun by stratagem captured Zou Si, distinguished those misled from the guilty, and only twelve were convicted of plotting.
translations.idiomatic: The court dispatched Wang Zhongke of the Court of Judicial Review to try the case. Tingyun devised a plan to capture Zou Si, sorted out those who had been misled from the true conspirators, and in the end only twelve were convicted of participation in the plot.

sentences.zh: 再調館陶主簿。

translations.literal: He was reassigned as chief clerk of Guantao.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as chief clerk of Guantao.

sentences.zh: 明昌元年三月，章宗諭旨學士院曰：「王庭筠所試文，句太長，朕不喜此，亦恐四方效之。

translations.literal: In the third month of the first year of Mingchang, Emperor Zhangzong instructed the Hanlin Academy: "In Wang Tingyun's examination essay the sentences are too long. I do not like this and fear the realm will imitate it."
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the first year of Mingchang, Emperor Zhangzong directed the Hanlin Academy: "Wang Tingyun's examination essay uses sentences that are too long. I dislike this, and I fear others across the realm will copy the fashion."

sentences.zh: 」又謂平章張汝霖曰：「王庭筠文藝頗佳，然語句不健，其人才高，亦不難改也。

translations.literal: He also told Grand Councilor Zhang Rulin: "Wang Tingyun's literary arts are quite fine, yet his phrasing lacks vigor. His talent is high — it would not be hard to correct."
translations.idiomatic: He also told Grand Councilor Zhang Rulin: "Wang Tingyun's literary gifts are considerable, but his phrasing lacks force. His talent is high, so it should not be difficult to correct."

sentences.zh: 」四月，召庭筠試館職，中選。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Tingyun was summoned to test for an academy post and passed selection.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Tingyun was summoned to compete for an academy post and was selected.

sentences.zh: 御史台言庭筠在館陶嘗犯贓罪，不當以館閣處之，遂罷。

translations.literal: The Censorate reported that while at Guantao Tingyun had once committed an offense of corruption and should not be placed in the academies; he was therefore dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate reported that Tingyun had once committed an offense involving bribery while serving at Guantao and was unfit for an academy post, and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 乃卜居彰德，買田隆慮，讀書黃華山寺，因以自號。

translations.literal: He then chose residence at Zhangde, bought land at Longlu, and studied at Mount Huanghua Temple, taking this as his sobriquet.
translations.idiomatic: He then settled at Zhangde, purchased land at Longlu, and devoted himself to study at Mount Huanghua Temple, adopting the mountain's name as his sobriquet.

sentences.zh: 是年十二月，上因語及學士，歎其乏材，參政守貞曰：「王庭筠其人也。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of that year, as the emperor spoke of academicians he lamented the lack of talent. Participating Councilor Shouzhen said: "Wang Tingyun is the man."
translations.idiomatic: That December, as the emperor spoke of academicians he lamented the dearth of talent. Participating Councilor Shouzhen said, "Wang Tingyun is your man."

sentences.zh: 」三年，召為應奉翰林文字，命與秘書郎張汝方品第法書、名畫，遂分入品者為五百五十卷。

translations.literal: In the third year he was summoned as Attendant Scribe of the Hanlin, ordered with Secretariat Gentleman Zhang Rufang to grade model calligraphy and famous paintings; those ranked as superior totaled five hundred fifty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was summoned to serve as Attendant Scribe of the Hanlin and, together with Secretariat Gentleman Zhang Rufang, was charged with grading model calligraphy and famous paintings; five hundred and fifty scrolls were classified as superior works.

sentences.zh: 五年八月，上顧謂宰執曰：「應奉王庭筠，朕欲以詔誥委之，其人才亦豈易得。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fifth year the emperor turned to the chief ministers and said: "Attendant Wang Tingyun — I wish to entrust edicts and proclamations to him. Such talent is not easily found."
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the fifth year the emperor addressed the chief ministers: "Attendant Wang Tingyun — I mean to entrust imperial edicts and proclamations to him. Talent like his is not easily found."

sentences.zh: 近党懷英作《長白山冊文》，殊不工。

translations.literal: Recently Dang Huaiying composed the Encomium for Mount Changbai, which was quite unskilled.
translations.idiomatic: Recently Dang Huaiying composed the Encomium for Mount Changbai, and the work was distinctly poor.

sentences.zh: 聞文士多妒庭筠者，不論其文，顧以行止為訾。

translations.literal: I hear many literary men are jealous of Tingyun; they do not judge his writing but instead fault his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: I hear that many men of letters are jealous of Tingyun; they do not judge his writing on its merits but attack his personal conduct instead.

sentences.zh: 大抵讀書人多口頰，或相黨。

translations.literal: Generally scholars have many mouths and cheeks — they form factions against one another.
translations.idiomatic: As a rule, scholars are quick with gossip and often band together in factions.

sentences.zh: 昔東漢之士與宦官分朋，固無足怪。

translations.literal: In former times Eastern Han scholars split into factions with eunuchs — that is hardly strange.
translations.idiomatic: In the Eastern Han, scholars and eunuchs formed rival factions — that is hardly surprising.

sentences.zh: 如唐牛僧孺、李德裕，宋司馬光、王安石，均為儒者，而互相排毀何耶。

translations.literal: Such as Tang's Niu Sengru and Li Deyu, Song's Sima Guang and Wang Anshi — all were Confucians, yet why did they mutually slander and destroy?
translations.idiomatic: Consider Tang's Niu Sengru and Li Deyu, or Song's Sima Guang and Wang Anshi — all were Confucian scholars, yet they tore one another down. Why should that be?

sentences.zh: 」遂遷庭筠為翰林修撰。

translations.literal: Tingyun was then promoted to Hanlin Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Tingyun was thereupon promoted to Hanlin Compiler.

sentences.zh: 承安元年正月，坐趙秉文上書事，削一官，杖六十，解職，語在秉文傳。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Cheng'an, implicated in Zhao Bingwen's memorial affair, he was stripped of one rank, beaten sixty strokes, and dismissed — as told in Bingwen's biography.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the first year of Cheng'an he was implicated in Zhao Bingwen's memorial affair, stripped of one rank, beaten sixty strokes, and dismissed from office — the full account appears in Bingwen's biography.

sentences.zh: 二年，降授鄭州防禦判官。

translations.literal: In the second year he was demoted and appointed Defense Adjutant of Zheng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was demoted to Defense Adjutant of Zheng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 四年，起為應奉翰林文字。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was reappointed Attendant Scribe of the Hanlin.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was recalled to serve as Attendant Scribe of the Hanlin.

sentences.zh: 泰和元年，複為翰林修撰，扈從秋山，應制賦詩三十餘首，上甚嘉之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taihe he was again made Hanlin Compiler, followed the autumn mountain tour, composed more than thirty poems on imperial command, and the emperor greatly praised them.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taihe he was again appointed Hanlin Compiler, accompanied the emperor on the autumn mountain tour, and composed more than thirty poems at imperial command, which the emperor greatly admired.

sentences.zh: 明年，卒，年四十有七。

translations.literal: The next year he died, aged forty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he died at the age of forty-seven.

sentences.zh: 上素知其貧，詔有司賻錢八十萬以給喪事，求生平詩文藏之秘閣。

translations.literal: The emperor had long known his poverty and ordered the authorities to grant eight hundred thousand in funeral funds and to seek his life's poems and writings for storage in the secret archive.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had long known how poor he was and ordered the authorities to grant eight hundred thousand cash for his funeral expenses and to collect his life's poems and prose for preservation in the imperial archive.

sentences.zh: 又以禦制詩賜其家，其引雲：「王遵古，朕之故人也。

translations.literal: He also bestowed an imperial poem on the family. Its preface read: "Wang Zungu was an old friend of mine."
translations.idiomatic: He also bestowed an imperial poem on the family, with a preface that read: "Wang Zungu was an old friend of mine."

sentences.zh: 乃子庭筠，複以才選直禁林者首尾十年，今茲雲亡，玉堂、東觀，無複斯人矣。」

translations.literal: His son Tingyun was again chosen for talent to serve in the Forbidden Grove for ten years in all. Now he has passed like clouds — in the Jade Hall and Eastern View there will be no such man again."
translations.idiomatic: His son Tingyun was again chosen for his talent to serve in the Forbidden Grove for a full decade. Now he has passed away, and in the Jade Hall and Eastern View there will never be such a man again."

sentences.zh: 庭筠儀觀秀偉，善談笑，外若簡貴，人初不敢與接。

translations.literal: Tingyun's bearing was handsome and imposing; he was skilled at banter and seemed outwardly aloof and noble, so at first people did not dare approach him.
translations.idiomatic: Tingyun was tall and striking in appearance, witty in conversation, and outwardly aloof and dignified, so at first people hesitated to approach him.

sentences.zh: 既見，和氣溢于顏間，殷勤慰藉如恐不及，少有可取極口稱道，他日雖百負不恨也。

translations.literal: Once met, warmth overflowed on his face; he comforted with earnest care as if fearing to fall short. The slightest merit he praised to the utmost; later even a hundred injuries he bore without resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Once you met him, warmth radiated from his face and he offered encouragement as though afraid he might not do enough. The smallest merit he praised to the skies, and even if you wronged him a hundred times later, he bore no grudge.

sentences.zh: 從游者如韓溫甫，路元亨、張進卿，李公度，其薦引者如趙秉文、馮璧、李純甫，皆一時名士，世以知人許之。

translations.literal: Those who studied with him such as Han Wenpu, Lu Yuanheng, Zhang Jinqing, and Li Gongdu; those he recommended such as Zhao Bingwen, Feng Bi, and Li Chunfu — all were famous men of the age. The world credited him with knowing men.
translations.idiomatic: Among those who studied under him were Han Wenpu, Lu Yuanheng, Zhang Jinqing, and Li Gongdu; among those he recommended were Zhao Bingwen, Feng Bi, and Li Chunfu — all celebrated figures of the day. The world acknowledged him as a judge of talent.

sentences.zh: 為文能道所欲言，暮年詩律深嚴，七言長篇尤工險韻。

translations.literal: In prose he could express whatever he wished to say. In his later years his poetic rules were deeply strict; he was especially skilled in long seven-character lines with difficult rhymes.
translations.idiomatic: In prose he could say exactly what he meant. In his later years his poetry grew rigorously disciplined, and he was especially masterful in long seven-character poems with demanding rhymes.

sentences.zh: 有《藂辨》十卷，文集四十卷。

translations.literal: He had ten juan of Collected Discriminations and forty juan of collected writings.
translations.idiomatic: He left ten juan of Collected Discriminations and forty juan of collected writings.

sentences.zh: 書法學米元章，與趙渢、趙秉文俱以名家，庭筠尤善山水墨竹雲。

translations.literal: In calligraphy he studied Mi Yuanzhang; with Zhao Feng and Zhao Bingwen he was all renowned masters, while Tingyun was especially skilled in landscape ink-bamboo and clouds.
translations.idiomatic: In calligraphy he studied Mi Fu; he, Zhao Feng, and Zhao Bingwen were all celebrated masters, while Tingyun was especially accomplished in landscape painting, ink bamboo, and clouds.

sentences.zh: 子曼慶，亦能詩並書，仕至行省右司郎中，自號「淡遊」雲。

translations.literal: His son Manqing could also compose poetry and write; he served to Director of the Right Office of a Branch Secretariat and styled himself "Leisurely Wanderer."
translations.idiomatic: His son Manqing was also accomplished in poetry and calligraphy, rose to Director of the Right Office of a Branch Secretariat, and styled himself "Leisurely Wanderer."

sentences.zh: 劉昂，字之昂，興州人。

translations.literal: Liu Ang, styled Zhi'ang, was a man of Xing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ang, whose style name was Zhi'ang, came from Xing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 大定十九年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the nineteenth year of Dading.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the nineteenth year of the Dading reign.

sentences.zh: 曾、高而下七世登科。

translations.literal: From his great-great-grandfather down through seven generations they passed the examinations.
translations.idiomatic: For seven generations, from his great-great-grandfather's line downward, his family had produced examination graduates.

sentences.zh: 昂天資警悟，律賦自成一家，作詩得晚唐體，尤工絕句。

translations.literal: Ang's natural gifts were keen and perceptive; his regulated fu formed a school of its own; in poetry he attained the late Tang manner and was especially skilled in quatrains.
translations.idiomatic: Ang was exceptionally quick-witted by nature; his regulated fu formed a distinctive school of its own; in poetry he mastered the late Tang style and was especially accomplished in quatrains.

sentences.zh: 李純甫《故人外傳》雲，昂早得仕，年三十三為尚書省掾，調平涼路轉運副使。

translations.literal: Li Chunfu's Unofficial Biographies of Old Friends says Ang entered office early; at thirty-three he was a clerk in the Department of State Affairs and was assigned Vice Transport Commissioner of Pingliang Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chunfu's Unofficial Biographies of Old Friends records that Ang entered government service early; at thirty-three he was a clerk in the Department of State Affairs and was posted as Vice Transport Commissioner of Pingliang Circuit.

sentences.zh: 時術士有言昂官止五品，昂不信。

translations.literal: At the time a diviner said Ang's office would stop at the fifth rank; Ang did not believe it.
translations.idiomatic: At the time a fortune-teller declared that Ang's official rank would never rise above the fifth grade, but Ang refused to believe it.

sentences.zh: 俄以母憂去職，連蹇十年，卜居洛陽，有終焉之志。

translations.literal: Soon he left office for mourning his mother; for ten years straight he met adversity, chose residence at Luoyang, and had the will to end his days there.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he left office to observe mourning for his mother, then spent a decade in repeated setbacks. He settled in Luoyang with the intention of ending his days there.

sentences.zh: 有薦其才于章宗者，泰和初，自國子司業擢為左司郎中。

translations.literal: Someone recommended his talent to Emperor Zhangzong; at the beginning of Taihe he was raised from Vice Director of the Directorate of Education to Left Department Director.
translations.idiomatic: Someone recommended his talent to Emperor Zhangzong, and at the beginning of the Taihe reign he was promoted from Vice Director of the Directorate of Education to Left Department Director.

sentences.zh: 會掌書大中與賈鉉漏言除授事，為言者所劾，獄辭連昂。

translations.literal: It happened that Director of Documents Dazhong and Jia Xuan leaked word of an appointment; remonstrators impeached them and the case records implicated Ang.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that Director of Documents Dazhong and Jia Xuan leaked word of a pending appointment; critics impeached them, and the case records implicated Ang as well.

sentences.zh: 章宗震怒。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhangzong was shaken with rage.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhangzong was furious.

sentences.zh: 一時聞人如史肅、李著、王宇、宗室從鬱皆譴逐之，鉉尋亦罷政。

translations.literal: At once renowned men such as Shi Su, Li Zhuo, Wang Yu, and the imperial clansman Congyu were all banished; Xuan soon left office as well.
translations.idiomatic: At once celebrated figures such as Shi Su, Li Zhuo, Wang Yu, and the imperial clansman Congyu were all banished, and Xuan soon left office as well.

sentences.zh: 昂降上京留守判官，道卒，竟如術者之言。

translations.literal: Ang was demoted to Adjutant of the Shangjing Military Commission; he died on the road, exactly as the diviner had said.
translations.idiomatic: Ang was demoted to Adjutant of the Shangjing Military Commission and died on the journey, exactly as the fortune-teller had predicted.

sentences.zh: 李經，字天英，錦州人。

translations.literal: Li Jing, styled Tianying, was a man of Jin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing, whose style name was Tianying, came from Jin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 作詩極刻苦，喜出奇語，不蹈襲前人。

translations.literal: In composing poetry he was extremely painstaking, delighted in startling phrases, and did not tread in the footsteps of predecessors.
translations.idiomatic: He composed poetry with extraordinary labor, delighted in startling turns of phrase, and refused to imitate his predecessors.

sentences.zh: 李純甫見其詩曰：「真今世太白也。

translations.literal: Li Chunfu, seeing his poems, said: "Truly the Libai of our age."
translations.idiomatic: When Li Chunfu read his poems he declared, "This is truly the Li Bai of our age."

sentences.zh: 」由是名大震。

translations.literal: From this his fame shook greatly.
translations.idiomatic: From that moment his fame spread far and wide.

sentences.zh: 再舉不第，拂衣去。

translations.literal: He failed the examination twice and shook out his robes and left.
translations.idiomatic: After failing the examinations twice, he shook the dust from his robes and walked away from official life.

sentences.zh: 南渡後，其鄉帥有表至朝廷，士大夫識之曰：「此天英筆也。

translations.literal: After the southern crossing, his district commander sent a memorial to court; scholar-officials recognized it and said: "This is Tianying's brush."
translations.idiomatic: After the court crossed south, his district commander sent a memorial to the court, and scholar-officials recognized it at once: "This is Tianying's hand."

sentences.zh: 」朝議以武功就命倅其州，後不知所終。

translations.literal: Court deliberation appointed him by military merit as vice-prefect of his prefecture; later his end was unknown.
translations.idiomatic: The court appointed him, on the strength of his military service, as vice-prefect of his home prefecture; afterward his fate is unknown.

sentences.zh: 劉從益

translations.literal: Liu Congyi
translations.idiomatic: Liu Congyi

sentences.zh: 劉從益，字雲卿，渾源人。

translations.literal: Liu Congyi, styled Yunqing, was a man of Hunyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Congyi, whose style name was Yunqing, came from Hunyuan.

sentences.zh: 其高祖捴，天會元年詞賦進士，子孫多由科第入仕。

translations.literal: His great-great-grandfather Cui was a jinshi in rhapsody and fu in the first year of Tianhui; descendants mostly entered office through the examinations.
translations.idiomatic: His great-great-grandfather Cui passed the rhapsody-and-fu jinshi examination in the first year of Tianhui, and for generations his descendants had entered government service through the civil examinations.

sentences.zh: 從益登大安元年進士第，累官監察御史，坐與當路辨曲直，得罪去。

translations.literal: Congyi passed the jinshi in the first year of Da'an, rose through offices to Investigating Censor, and for arguing right and wrong with those in power offended and left.
translations.idiomatic: Congyi passed the jinshi examination in the first year of Da'an, rose through the ranks to Investigating Censor, and was dismissed after disputing right and wrong with those in power.

sentences.zh: 久之，起為葉縣令，修學勵俗，有古良吏風。

translations.literal: After a long while he was reappointed magistrate of Ye County, cultivated learning and encouraged custom, and had the manner of the good officials of old.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was reappointed magistrate of Ye County, where he promoted learning and moral reform in the manner of the exemplary officials of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 葉自兵興，戶減三之一，田不毛者萬七千畝有奇，其歲入七萬石如故。

translations.literal: Since war arose in Ye, households fell by one third; uncultivated fields exceeded seventeen thousand mu, yet the annual levy remained seventy thousand shi as before.
translations.idiomatic: Since the outbreak of war, Ye had lost a third of its households, and more than seventeen thousand mu of land lay fallow, yet the annual tax levy still stood at seventy thousand shi, unchanged from before.

sentences.zh: 從益請于大司農，為減一萬，民甚賴之，流亡歸者四千餘家。

translations.literal: Congyi petitioned the Grand Minister of Agriculture to reduce it by ten thousand; the people relied greatly on this, and more than four thousand refugee households returned.
translations.idiomatic: Congyi petitioned the Grand Minister of Agriculture to reduce the levy by ten thousand shi. The people depended greatly on this relief, and more than four thousand refugee households returned.

sentences.zh: 未幾，被召，百姓詣尚書省乞留，不聽。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned; the people went to the Department of State Affairs begging to keep him, but the request was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was summoned to the capital. The people went to the Department of State Affairs to beg that he be kept in office, but their plea was denied.

sentences.zh: 入授應奉翰林文字，逾月以疾卒，年四十四。

translations.literal: He entered and was appointed Attendant Scribe of the Hanlin; after more than a month he died of illness, aged forty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital and was appointed Attendant Scribe of the Hanlin, but a little more than a month later he died of illness at the age of forty-four.

sentences.zh: 葉人聞之，以端午罷酒為位而哭，且立石頌德，以致哀思。

translations.literal: When the people of Ye heard, they suspended wine on the Dragon Boat Festival and set up a place to weep, and also erected a stone praising his virtue to express mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When the people of Ye heard the news, they abstained from wine on the Dragon Boat Festival and gathered to mourn him, and they erected a stone inscription praising his virtue to express their grief.

sentences.zh: 從益博學強記，精于經學。

translations.literal: Congyi was broadly learned with a powerful memory and excelled in classical studies.
translations.idiomatic: Congyi was broadly learned with an exceptional memory and was a master of the Confucian classics.

sentences.zh: 為文章長於詩，五言尤工，有《蓬門集》。

translations.literal: In writing he excelled at poetry; five-character verse was especially skilled. He had Collected Works of the Humble Gate.
translations.idiomatic: As a writer he excelled in poetry, especially five-character verse. He left a collection entitled Works from the Humble Gate.

sentences.zh: 子祁字京叔。

translations.literal: His son Qi was styled Jingshu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qi was styled Jingshu.

sentences.zh: 為太學生。

translations.literal: He was a student of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was a student at the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 甚有文名。

translations.literal: He had great literary renown.
translations.idiomatic: He enjoyed considerable literary renown.

sentences.zh: 值金末喪亂，作《歸潛志》以紀金事，修《金史》多採用焉。

translations.literal: At the end of Jin amid calamity and disorder he composed Returning to Seclusion to record Jin affairs; compiling the History of Jin drew heavily upon it.
translations.idiomatic: At the collapse of the Jin dynasty he wrote Returning to Seclusion to record events of the Jin era, and the compilers of the History of Jin drew heavily upon it.

sentences.zh: 呂中孚 張建

translations.literal: Lü Zhongfu and Zhang Jian
translations.idiomatic: Lü Zhongfu and Zhang Jian

sentences.zh: 呂中孚，字信臣，冀州南宮人。

translations.literal: Lü Zhongfu, styled Xinchen, was a man of Nangong in Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Zhongfu, whose style name was Xinchen, came from Nangong in Ji Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 張建字吉甫，蒲城人。

translations.literal: Zhang Jian, styled Jifu, was a man of Pucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jian, whose style name was Jifu, came from Pucheng.

sentences.zh: 皆有詩名。

translations.literal: Both had renown in poetry.
translations.idiomatic: Both enjoyed a reputation as poets.

sentences.zh: 中孚有《清漳集》。

translations.literal: Zhongfu had Collected Works of Clear Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfu left the Collected Works of Clear Zhang.

sentences.zh: 建明昌初授絳州教官，召為宮教、應奉翰林文字。

translations.literal: Jian in the early Mingchang era was appointed instructor of Jiang Prefecture, then summoned as palace instructor and Attendant Scribe of the Hanlin.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Mingchang era Jian was appointed instructor of Jiang Prefecture, then summoned to serve as palace instructor and Attendant Scribe of the Hanlin.

sentences.zh: 以老請致仕，章宗愛其純素，不欲令去，授同知華州防禦使，仍賜詩以寵之。

translations.literal: He requested retirement on grounds of age; Emperor Zhangzong loved his plain purity and did not wish him to leave, appointing him Vice Commissioner of Huazhou Defense while still bestowing a poem to honor him.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to retire on account of age. Emperor Zhangzong admired his plain, unadorned character and did not wish to let him go, appointing him Vice Commissioner of Huazhou Defense while still bestowing an imperial poem to honor him.

sentences.zh: 自號「蘭泉」，有集行於世。

translations.literal: He styled himself "Orchid Spring" and had a collection circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He styled himself "Orchid Spring," and his collected works circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 李純甫

translations.literal: Li Chunfu
translations.idiomatic: Li Chunfu

sentences.zh: 李純甫，字之純，弘州襄陰人。

translations.literal: Li Chunfu, styled Zhichun, was a man of Xiangyin in Hong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chunfu, whose style name was Zhichun, came from Xiangyin in Hong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祖安上，嘗魁西京進士。

translations.literal: His grandfather Anshang had once topped the Western Capital jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Anshang had once placed first in the jinshi examination at the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 父采，卒於益都府治中。

translations.literal: His father Cai died while serving as administrative aide of Yidu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Cai died while serving as administrative aide of Yidu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 純甫幼穎悟異常，初業詞賦，及讀《左氏春秋》，大愛之，遂更為經義學。

translations.literal: Chunfu in youth was unusually quick-witted; he first studied rhapsody and fu, but upon reading the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals he greatly loved it and thereupon switched to classical exegesis.
translations.idiomatic: Chunfu was exceptionally quick-witted as a youth. He first studied rhapsody and fu, but when he read the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals he fell deeply in love with it and switched to the study of classical exegesis.

sentences.zh: 擢承安二年經義進士。

translations.literal: He was selected as a jinshi in classical exegesis in the second year of Cheng'an.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in classical exegesis in the second year of Cheng'an.

sentences.zh: 為文法莊周、列禦寇、左氏、《戰國策》，後進多宗之。

translations.literal: In writing he took Zhuangzi, Lie Yukou, the Zuo Commentary, and the Stratagems of the Warring States as his models; younger writers mostly followed him.
translations.idiomatic: As a writer he modeled himself on Zhuangzi, Lie Yukou, the Zuo Commentary, and the Stratagems of the Warring States, and younger writers largely followed his example.

sentences.zh: 又喜談兵，慨然有經世心。

translations.literal: He also delighted in discussing military affairs and ardently harbored a mind to order the age.
translations.idiomatic: He also delighted in military affairs and burned with a desire to put the world in order.

sentences.zh: 章宗南征，兩上疏策其勝負，上奇之，給送軍中，後多如所料。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhangzong campaigned south, he twice submitted memorials forecasting victory and defeat; the emperor marveled at this and had them sent to the army — later events largely matched his predictions.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhangzong campaigned south, Chunfu twice submitted memorials forecasting the outcome; the emperor was impressed and had them forwarded to the army, and later events largely matched his predictions.

sentences.zh: 宰執愛其文，薦入翰林。

translations.literal: The chief ministers loved his writing and recommended him into the Hanlin.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers admired his writing and recommended him for the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 及大元兵起，又上疏論時事，不報。

translations.literal: When the Great Yuan armies rose, he again submitted a memorial on current affairs, but received no response.
translations.idiomatic: When the armies of the Great Yuan rose, he again submitted a memorial on current affairs, but received no response.

sentences.zh: 宣宗遷汴，再入翰林。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong moved the capital to Bian, Chunfu again entered the Hanlin.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong moved the capital to Bian, Chunfu again entered the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 時丞相高琪擅威福柄，擢為左司都事，純甫審其必敗，以母老辭去。

translations.literal: At the time Grand Councilor Gao Qi monopolized power; he promoted Chunfu to Director of the Left Department, but Chunfu judged that Qi would surely fall and declined on the grounds that his mother was old.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Grand Councilor Gao Qi monopolized power and promoted Chunfu to Director of the Left Department, but Chunfu saw that Qi would surely fall and declined on the grounds that his mother was elderly.

sentences.zh: 既而高琪誅，複入翰林，連知貢舉。

translations.literal: Soon after Qi was executed, Chunfu re-entered the Hanlin and successively oversaw the civil examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after Qi was executed, Chunfu returned to the Hanlin and successively oversaw the civil examinations.

sentences.zh: 正大末，坐取人逾新格，出倅坊州。

translations.literal: At the end of the Zhengda era, for taking candidates beyond the new quota he was demoted to vice-prefect of Fang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Zhengda era he was demoted to vice-prefect of Fang Prefecture for accepting candidates beyond the new quota.

sentences.zh: 未赴，改京兆府判官。

translations.literal: Before he took up the post he was reassigned as administrative judge of the Jingzhao metropolitan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the post he was reassigned as administrative judge of the Jingzhao metropolitan prefecture.

sentences.zh: 卒於汴，年四十七。

translations.literal: He died at Bian, aged forty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died at Bian at the age of forty-seven.

sentences.zh: 純甫為人聰敏，少自負其材，謂功名可俯拾，作《矮柏賦》，以諸葛孔明、王景略自期。

translations.literal: Chunfu was clever by nature; in youth he was confident in his talent and believed success and fame could be picked up at will. He wrote "Rhapsody on the Dwarf Cypress," taking Zhuge Liang and Wang Meng as his models.
translations.idiomatic: By nature Chunfu was brilliant. In youth he was confident in his own gifts and believed that fame and office lay within easy reach. He wrote the "Rhapsody on the Dwarf Cypress," measuring himself against Zhuge Liang and Wang Meng.

sentences.zh: 由小官上萬方書，援宋為證，甚切，當路者以迂闊見抑。

translations.literal: From a minor post he submitted a Ten Thousand Directions Memorial, citing Song as proof in terms very urgent; those in power suppressed him as impractical and broad.
translations.idiomatic: From a minor post he submitted a memorial addressed to all directions, citing Song as a precedent in urgent terms; those in power dismissed him as impractical and utopian.

sentences.zh: 中年，度其道不行，益 縱酒自放，無仕進意。

translations.literal: In midlife, seeing his path would not prevail, he all the more gave himself to drink and self-abandonment, with no mind for advancement.
translations.idiomatic: In midlife, seeing that his path would not prevail, he gave himself ever more to drink and reckless freedom, with no further desire for office.

sentences.zh: 得官未成考，旋即歸隱。

translations.literal: He gained office but had not completed his term evaluation when he at once returned to seclusion.
translations.idiomatic: He gained office but had not yet completed his term evaluation when he at once withdrew into seclusion.

sentences.zh: 日與禪僧士子游，以文酒為事，嘯歌袒裼出禮法外，或飲數月不醒。

translations.literal: Day after day he wandered with Chan monks and scholars, making literature and wine his business; singing loudly and baring his torso beyond the bounds of ritual, at times he drank for months without sobering.
translations.idiomatic: Day after day he kept company with Chan monks and scholars, devoting himself to wine and letters; singing loudly and casting off his robes beyond the bounds of propriety, he sometimes drank for months without sobering.

sentences.zh: 人有酒見招，不擇貴賤必往，往輒醉，雖沉醉亦未嘗廢著書。

translations.literal: Whenever anyone invited him for drink, he went without choosing between noble and humble; he always went and always got drunk, yet even in deep intoxication he never ceased writing.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever anyone invited him to drink, he went without regard to rank; he always went and always got drunk, yet even in deep intoxication he never stopped writing.

sentences.zh: 然晚年喜佛，力探其奧義。

translations.literal: Yet in his later years he delighted in Buddhism and strove to probe its deepest meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in his later years he turned to Buddhism and strove to probe its deepest meaning.

sentences.zh: 自類其文，凡論性理及關佛老二家者號「內稿」，其餘應物文字為「外稿」。

translations.literal: He classified his own writings: those discussing human nature and the two schools of Buddhism and Daoism he called "inner drafts"; the rest, writings responding to affairs, were "outer drafts."
translations.idiomatic: He classified his own writings: pieces on human nature and on Buddhism and Daoism he called "inner drafts," while everything else written in response to worldly affairs he called "outer drafts."

sentences.zh: 又解《楞嚴》、《金剛經》、《老子》、《莊子》。

translations.literal: He also wrote commentaries on the Shurangama Sutra, the Diamond Sutra, the Laozi, and the Zhuangzi.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote commentaries on the Shurangama Sutra, the Diamond Sutra, the Laozi, and the Zhuangzi.

sentences.zh: 又有《中庸集解》、《鳴道集解》，號「中國心學、西方文教」。

translations.literal: He also had Collected Commentaries on the Doctrine of the Mean and Collected Commentaries on the Way of the Mings, styled "Heart Learning of China, Literary Teaching of the West."
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Collected Commentaries on the Doctrine of the Mean and Collected Commentaries on the Way of the Mings, which he styled "Heart Learning of China, Literary Teaching of the West."

sentences.zh: 數十萬言，以故為名教所貶雲。

translations.literal: Several hundred thousand characters in all; for this reason he was disparaged by orthodox teaching.
translations.idiomatic: They ran to several hundred thousand characters, and for this reason he was disparaged by orthodox Confucian teaching.

sentences.zh: 王郁，字飛伯，大興人。

translations.literal: Wang Yu, styled Feibo, was a man of Daxing.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yu, whose style name was Feibo, came from Daxing.

sentences.zh: 儀狀魁奇，目光如鶻。

translations.literal: His bearing was striking and imposing; his gaze was like a falcon's.
translations.idiomatic: He was striking in stature, with a gaze sharp as a falcon's.

sentences.zh: 少居釣台，閉門讀書，不接人事。

translations.literal: In youth he lived at Fishing Terrace, reading behind closed doors and having no dealings with the world.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he lived at Fishing Terrace, reading behind closed doors and refusing all worldly entanglements.

sentences.zh: 久之，為文法柳宗元，閎肆奇古，動輒數千言。

translations.literal: After a long while, in writing he took Liu Zongyuan as his model — vast, bold, strange, and ancient, often running to several thousand characters.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he took Liu Zongyuan as his literary model, writing in a vast, bold, and archaic style that often ran to several thousand characters.

sentences.zh: 歌詩俊逸，效李白。

translations.literal: His songs and poems were elegant and free, in the manner of Li Bai.
translations.idiomatic: His songs and poems were elegant and uninhibited, in the manner of Li Bai.

sentences.zh: 嘗作《王子小傳》以自敘。

translations.literal: He once wrote a "Little Biography of the Prince" as self-narration.
translations.idiomatic: He once wrote a "Little Biography of the Prince" as an autobiographical sketch.

sentences.zh: 天興初元，汴京被圍，上書言事，不報。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Tianxing era, when Bianjing was besieged, he submitted a memorial on affairs but received no response.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Tianxing era, when Bianjing was besieged, he submitted a memorial on public affairs but received no response.

sentences.zh: 四月，圍稍解，挺身突出，為兵士所得。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, as the siege eased somewhat, he thrust himself out and was seized by soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, when the siege had eased somewhat, he forced his way out and was seized by soldiers.

sentences.zh: 其將遇之甚厚，鬱經行無機防，為其下所忌，見殺。

translations.literal: The commander treated him very generously, but Yu traveled without precaution and was resented by subordinates and killed.
translations.idiomatic: The commander treated him with great generosity, but Yu traveled without precaution and was resented by his subordinates and killed.

sentences.zh: 臨終，懷中出書曰：「是吾平生著述，可傳付中州士大夫曰，王鬱死矣。

translations.literal: At the end he drew writings from his breast and said: "These are my life's compositions. They may be passed to the scholar-officials of the Central Plains with the message that Wang Yu is dead."
translations.idiomatic: At the end he drew writings from his breast and said, "These are my life's compositions. Pass them to the scholar-officials of the Central Plains with the message that Wang Yu is dead."

sentences.zh: 」年三十餘。

translations.literal: He was a little over thirty.
translations.idiomatic: He was a little over thirty years old.

sentences.zh: 同時以詩鳴者，雷琯、侯冊、王元粹雲。

translations.literal: Those who at the same time were famed in poetry included Lei Guan, Hou Ce, and Wang Yuancui.
translations.idiomatic: Those famed in poetry at the same time included Lei Guan, Hou Ce, and Wang Yuancui.

sentences.zh: 宋九嘉

translations.literal: Song Jiujia
translations.idiomatic: Song Jiujia

sentences.zh: 龐鑄，字才卿，遼東人。

translations.literal: Pang Zhu, styled Caiqing, was a man of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Zhu, whose style name was Caiqing, came from Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 少擢第，仕有聲。

translations.literal: He passed the examinations young and served with renown.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the examinations at a young age and served with distinction.

sentences.zh: 南渡後，為翰林待制，遷戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: After the southern crossing he was Hanlin Attendant-in-Waiting and was promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: After the court crossed south he served as Hanlin Attendant-in-Waiting and was promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 坐游貴戚家，出倅東平，改京兆路轉運使，卒。

translations.literal: For visiting the house of an imperial in-law he was demoted to vice-prefect of Dongping, then reassigned as transport commissioner of the Jingzhao Circuit, and died.
translations.idiomatic: For visiting the house of an imperial in-law he was demoted to vice-prefect of Dongping, then reassigned as transport commissioner of the Jingzhao Circuit, where he died.

sentences.zh: 博學能文，工詩，造語奇健不凡，世多傳之。

translations.literal: Broadly learned and able in letters, skilled in poetry, his phrasing was striking, vigorous, and uncommon; the age widely transmitted his works.
translations.idiomatic: He was broadly learned and accomplished in letters, skilled in poetry, with phrasing that was striking, vigorous, and uncommon; his works circulated widely in his day.

sentences.zh: 李獻能

translations.literal: Li Xianneng
translations.idiomatic: Li Xianneng

sentences.zh: 李獻能，字欽叔，河中人。

translations.literal: Li Xianneng, styled Qinshu, was a man of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xianneng, whose style name was Qinshu, came from Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 先世有為金吾衛上將軍者，時號「李金吾家」。

translations.literal: In former generations someone had served as general of the Jinwu Guard; at the time they were called "the Li family of the Jinwu Guard."
translations.idiomatic: His forebears had included a general of the Jinwu Guard, and the family was known in its day as "the Li household of the Jinwu Guard."

sentences.zh: 迨獻能昆弟皆以文學名，從兄獻卿、獻誠、從弟獻甫相繼擢第，故李氏有「四桂堂」。

translations.literal: By the time Xianneng and his brothers were all famed in letters, his elder cousin Xianqing, Xianqing's brother Xiancheng, and his younger cousin Xianfu passed the examinations in succession, so the Li family had the "Hall of Four Cassia."
translations.idiomatic: By the time Xianneng and his brothers were all famed for literature, his elder cousin Xianqing, Xianqing's brother Xiancheng, and his younger cousin Xianfu passed the examinations in succession, earning the Li family the name "Hall of Four Cassia."

sentences.zh: 獻能苦學博覽，于文尤長於四六。

translations.literal: Xianneng studied laboriously with wide reading; in letters he was especially skilled in parallel prose.
translations.idiomatic: Xianneng studied with arduous labor and wide reading; in letters he was especially accomplished in parallel prose.

sentences.zh: 貞祐三年，特賜詞賦進士，廷試第一人，宏詞優等。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenyou he was specially granted the jinshi in rhapsody and fu, placed first in the palace examination, and rated superior in the macro-rhapsody.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenyou he was specially granted the jinshi in rhapsody and fu, placed first in the palace examination, and rated superior in the macro-rhapsody competition.

sentences.zh: 授應奉翰林文字。

translations.literal: He was appointed Attendant Scribe of the Hanlin.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Attendant Scribe of the Hanlin.

sentences.zh: 在翰苑凡十年，出為鄜州觀察判官。

translations.literal: He spent ten years in the Hanlin altogether, then left to serve as administrative judge of the Zouzhou observation commission.
translations.idiomatic: He spent ten years in the Hanlin altogether, then left office to serve as administrative judge of the Zouzhou observation commission.

sentences.zh: 用薦者複為應奉，俄遷修撰。

translations.literal: On recommendation he was again made an attendant; soon he was promoted to compiler.
translations.idiomatic: On recommendation he was again made an attendant scribe; soon he was promoted to compiler.

sentences.zh: 正大末，以鎮南軍節度副使充河中帥府經歷官。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhengda he served as military vice commissioner of the Zhennan Army and staff officer of the Hezhong commandery headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Zhengda era he served as military vice commissioner of the Zhennan Army and staff officer at the Hezhong commandery headquarters.

sentences.zh: 大元兵破河中，奔陝州，行省以郐雚左右司郎中，值趙三三軍變遇害，年四十三。

translations.literal: When the Great Yuan army took Hezhong he fled to Shaan Prefecture; the branch secretariat appointed him Left Department Director, and he was killed in the mutiny of Zhao Sansan's army, aged forty-three.
translations.idiomatic: When the Great Yuan army captured Hezhong he fled to Shaan Prefecture. The branch secretariat appointed him Left Department Director, but he was killed in the mutiny of Zhao Sansan's army at the age of forty-three.

sentences.zh: 獻能為人眇小而黑色，頗有髯。

translations.literal: Xianneng was small in stature and dark in complexion, with a rather full beard.
translations.idiomatic: Xianneng was slight in build and dark in complexion, with a rather full beard.

sentences.zh: 善談論，每敷說今古，聲鏗亮可聽。

translations.literal: He was skilled at discourse; whenever he expounded past and present, his voice rang clear and was pleasant to hear.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at discourse; whenever he expounded past and present affairs, his voice rang clear and was a pleasure to hear.

sentences.zh: 作詩有志于風雅，又刻意樂章。

translations.literal: In poetry he aspired to the Airs and Elegances and also devoted himself painstakingly to song lyrics.
translations.idiomatic: In poetry he aspired to the standards of the Airs and Elegances and also devoted himself painstakingly to song lyrics.

sentences.zh: 在翰院，應機敏捷號得體。

translations.literal: In the Hanlin he was nimble in meeting occasions and was called apt in deportment.
translations.idiomatic: In the Hanlin he was nimble in meeting occasions and was praised for apt deportment.

sentences.zh: 趙秉文、李純甫嘗曰：「李獻能天生今世翰苑材。

translations.literal: Zhao Bingwen and Li Chunfu once said: "Li Xianneng is Heaven's gift of Hanlin talent for our age."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Bingwen and Li Chunfu once said, "Li Xianneng is a Hanlin talent sent by Heaven for our age."

sentences.zh: 」故每薦之，不令出館。

translations.literal: Therefore they always recommended him and would not let him leave the academy.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore they always recommended him and would not allow him to leave the academy.

sentences.zh: 家故饒財，盡於貞祐之亂，在京師無以自資。

translations.literal: His family had once been wealthy, but everything was lost in the disorders of Zhenyou; in the capital he had no means to support himself.
translations.idiomatic: His family had once been wealthy, but everything was lost in the disorders of Zhenyou, and in the capital he had no means to support himself.

sentences.zh: 其母素豪奢，厚於自奉，小不如意則必訶譴，人視之殆不堪憂，獻能處之自若也。

translations.literal: His mother had always been extravagant, indulging herself generously; at the slightest displeasure she would surely scold and reproach. Others regarded this as nearly unbearable, yet Xianneng bore it with complete composure.
translations.idiomatic: His mother had always been extravagant and indulged herself generously; at the slightest displeasure she would scold and reproach him. Others thought this nearly unbearable, yet Xianneng bore it with complete composure.

sentences.zh: 時人以純孝稱之。

translations.literal: People of the time praised him for pure filial devotion.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time praised him for pure filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂人雲：「吾幼夢官至五品，壽不至五十。

translations.literal: He once told others: "In youth I dreamed that my office would reach the fifth rank and my life would not pass fifty."
translations.idiomatic: He once told others, "In youth I dreamed that my office would reach the fifth rank and that I would not live past fifty."

sentences.zh: 」後竟如其言。

translations.literal: Later it turned out exactly as he had said.
translations.idiomatic: In the end it turned out exactly as he had said.

sentences.zh: 王若虛

translations.literal: Wang Ruoxu
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ruoxu

sentences.zh: 王若虛，字從之，槁城人也。

translations.literal: Wang Ruoxu, styled Congzhi, was a man of Gaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ruoxu, whose style name was Congzhi, came from Gaocheng.

sentences.zh: 幼穎悟，若夙昔在文字間者。

translations.literal: In youth he was quick-witted, as if he had always dwelt among written words.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a child he was quick-witted, as though he had always lived among written words.

sentences.zh: 擢承安二年經義進士。

translations.literal: He was selected as a jinshi in classical exegesis in the second year of Cheng'an.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in classical exegesis in the second year of Cheng'an.

sentences.zh: 調鄜州錄事，曆管城、門山二縣令，皆有惠政，秩滿，老幼攀送，數日乃得行。

translations.literal: He was assigned recorder of Zou Prefecture and successively served as magistrate of Guancheng and Menshan, in each place enacting benevolent rule; when his term ended, old and young clung to send him off and several days passed before he could depart.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned recorder of Zou Prefecture and successively served as magistrate of Guancheng and Menshan, enacting benevolent policies in each place. When his terms ended, old and young clung to him in farewell, and several days passed before he could take his leave.

sentences.zh: 用薦入為國史院編修官，遷應奉翰林文字。

translations.literal: On recommendation he entered as compiler in the Institute of National History and was promoted to Attendant Scribe of the Hanlin.
translations.idiomatic: On recommendation he entered the Institute of National History as a compiler and was promoted to Attendant Scribe of the Hanlin.

sentences.zh: 奉使夏國，還授同知泗州軍州事，留為著作佐郎。

translations.literal: Sent as envoy to Western Xia, on his return he was appointed Vice Commissioner of Sizhou and retained as Assistant in the Office of Writings.
translations.idiomatic: After serving as envoy to Western Xia, he was appointed Vice Commissioner of Sizhou and retained as Assistant in the Office of Writings.

sentences.zh: 正大初，《宣宗實錄》成，遷平涼府判官。

translations.literal: In the early Zhengda era, when the Veritable Records of Emperor Xuanzong were completed, he was promoted to administrative judge of Pingliang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Zhengda era, when the Veritable Records of Emperor Xuanzong were completed, he was promoted to administrative judge of Pingliang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 未幾，召為左司諫，後轉延州刺史，入為直學士。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned as Left Department Remonstrator, later transferred to prefect of Yan Prefecture, then entered as Academician Expositor.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was summoned as Left Department Remonstrator, later transferred to prefect of Yan Prefecture, then entered service as Academician Expositor.

sentences.zh: 元興元年，哀宗走歸德。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanxing, Emperor Aizong fled to Guide.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanxing, Emperor Aizong fled to Guide.

sentences.zh: 明年春，崔立變。

translations.literal: The next spring, Cui Li mutinied.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring, Cui Li mutinied.

sentences.zh: 群小附和，請為立建功德碑，翟奕以尚書省命召若虛為文。

translations.literal: Petty men rallied to him and requested a merit stele for Li; Zhai Yi, on orders of the Department of State Affairs, summoned Ruoxu to compose the text.
translations.idiomatic: Petty men rallied to him and requested a merit stele for Li; Zhai Yi, acting on orders from the Department of State Affairs, summoned Ruoxu to compose the text.

sentences.zh: 時奕輩恃勢作威，人或少忤，則讒構立見屠滅。

translations.literal: At the time Yi and his faction relied on power to act arrogantly; anyone who slightly crossed them would be slandered and at once slaughtered.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Yi and his faction relied on power to act arrogantly; anyone who slightly crossed them would be slandered and at once put to death.

sentences.zh: 若虛自分必死，私謂左右司員外郎元好問曰：「今召我作碑，不從則死。

translations.literal: Ruoxu judged that he would surely die and privately told Left and Right Department Vice Director Yuan Haowen: "Now they summon me to make a stele; if I refuse I die."
translations.idiomatic: Ruoxu judged that he would surely die and privately told Left and Right Department Vice Director Yuan Haowen, "Now they summon me to write a stele; if I refuse, I die."

sentences.zh: 作之則名節掃地，不若死之為愈。

translations.literal: If I write it, my integrity will be swept clean — better to die.
translations.idiomatic: If I write it, my reputation for integrity will be destroyed — better to die.

sentences.zh: 雖然，我姑以理諭之。

translations.literal: Even so, I shall for the moment try to persuade them with reason.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, I shall for the moment try to persuade them with reason.

sentences.zh: 」乃謂奕輩曰：「丞相功德碑當指何事為言？

translations.literal: He then said to Yi and the rest: "A merit stele for the Grand Councilor — what affair should it speak of?"
translations.idiomatic: He then said to Yi and the rest, "A merit stele for the Grand Councilor — what affair should it speak of?"

sentences.zh: 」奕輩怒曰：「丞相以京城降，活生靈百萬，非功德乎？

translations.literal: Yi and the rest angrily said: "The Grand Councilor surrendered the capital and saved a million lives — is that not merit?"
translations.idiomatic: Yi and the rest said angrily, "The Grand Councilor surrendered the capital and saved a million lives — is that not merit?"

translations.literal: He said:
translations.idiomatic: Ruoxu said:

sentences.zh: 「學士代王言，功德碑謂之代王言可乎？

translations.literal: "An academician speaks for the king — can a merit stele be called speaking for the king?"
translations.idiomatic: "An academician speaks for the king — can a merit stele be called speaking for the king?"

sentences.zh: 且丞相既以城降，則朝官皆出其門，自古豈有門下人為主帥誦功德而可信乎後世哉？

translations.literal: Moreover, since the Grand Councilor has already surrendered the city, all court officials came from his gate — since antiquity has there ever been a case in which men of one's own faction sang the merits of their commander and could be trusted by posterity?"
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, since the Grand Councilor has already surrendered the city, all court officials came from his faction — since antiquity has there ever been a case in which a commander's own followers composed his merit stele and could be trusted by posterity?"

sentences.zh: 」奕輩不能奪，乃召太學生劉祁、麻革輩赴省，好問、張信之喻以立碑事，曰：「眾議屬二君，且已白鄭王矣，二君其無讓。

translations.literal: Yi and the rest could not overcome him and therefore summoned Imperial Academy students Liu Qi, Ma Ge, and others to the secretariat; Haowen and Zhang Xinzhi explained the stele affair to them, saying: "Public opinion assigns this to you two, and it has already been reported to Prince Zheng — do not decline."
translations.idiomatic: Yi and the rest could not overcome him and therefore summoned Imperial Academy students Liu Qi, Ma Ge, and others to the secretariat. Haowen and Zhang Xinzhi explained the stele affair to them, saying, "Public opinion assigns this to you two, and it has already been reported to Prince Zheng — you must not decline."

sentences.zh: 」祁等固辭而別。

translations.literal: Qi and the rest firmly declined and left.
translations.idiomatic: Qi and the rest firmly declined and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 數日，促迫不已，祁即為草定，以付好問，好問意未愜，乃自為之。

translations.literal: After several days of unceasing pressure, Qi at once drafted a version and handed it to Haowen; Haowen was not satisfied and wrote it himself.
translations.idiomatic: After several days of unceasing pressure, Qi at once drafted a version and handed it to Haowen, but Haowen was not satisfied and wrote it himself.

sentences.zh: 既成，以示若虛，乃共刪定數字，然止直敘其事而已。

translations.literal: When it was finished it was shown to Ruoxu, and together they revised a few characters, yet in the end they only stated the facts plainly.
translations.idiomatic: When it was finished it was shown to Ruoxu, and together they revised a few characters, yet in the end they only stated the facts plainly.

sentences.zh: 後兵入城，不果立也。

translations.literal: Later the army entered the city and the stele was not erected after all.
translations.idiomatic: Later the army entered the city, and the stele was never erected.

sentences.zh: 金亡，微服北歸鎮陽，與渾源劉郁東游泰山，至黃峴峰，憩萃美亭，顧謂同遊曰：「汩沒塵土中一生，不意晚年乃造仙府，誠得終老此山，志願畢矣。

translations.literal: When Jin fell, he traveled north in plain dress to Zhenyang and, with Liu Yu of Hunyuan, toured Mount Tai eastward to Yellow Xian Peak, resting at the Gathering Beauty Pavilion. He turned to his companions and said: "Sunk in dust all my life — I never expected in my later years to reach this immortal realm. If I could end my days on this mountain, my wish would be fulfilled."
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of Jin he traveled north in plain dress to Zhenyang and, with Liu Yu of Hunyuan, toured Mount Tai to Yellow Xian Peak, where he rested at the Gathering Beauty Pavilion. He turned to his companions and said, "I spent my whole life sunk in the dust of the world — I never expected in my later years to reach this immortal realm. If I could end my days on this mountain, my wish would be fulfilled."

sentences.zh: 」乃令子忠先歸，遣子恕前行視夷險，因垂足坐大石上，良久瞑目而逝，年七十。

translations.literal: He then sent his son Zhong home first and dispatched his son Shu ahead to survey the terrain, then let his feet hang and sat on a great rock; after a long while he closed his eyes and passed away, aged seventy.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent his son Zhong home first and dispatched his son Shu ahead to survey the route, then sat on a great rock with his feet hanging over the edge. After a long while he closed his eyes and passed away at the age of seventy.

sentences.zh: 所著文章號《慵夫集》若干卷、《滹南遺老》若干卷、傳於世。

translations.literal: His writings were titled Collected Works of the Idle Man in several juan and Old Man of the South of the Hu in several juan, transmitted in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His writings included the Collected Works of the Idle Man and Old Man of the South of the Hu, each in several juan, which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 王元節

translations.literal: Wang Yuanjie
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuanjie

sentences.zh: 王元節，字子元，弘州人也。

translations.literal: Wang Yuanjie, styled Ziyuan, was a man of Hong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuanjie, whose style name was Ziyuan, came from Hong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祖山甫，遼戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shanfu was Vice Minister of Revenue in Liao.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shanfu had served as Vice Minister of Revenue under the Liao.

sentences.zh: 父詡，海陵朝，左司員外郎。

translations.literal: His father Xu, in the Hailing era, was Vice Director of the Left Department.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xu, in the Hailing reign, served as Vice Director of the Left Department.

sentences.zh: 元節幼穎悟，雖家世貴顯，而從學甚謹。

translations.literal: Yuanjie in youth was quick-witted; though his family was illustrious, he studied with great care.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjie was quick-witted as a youth; though his family was illustrious, he pursued his studies with great diligence.

sentences.zh: 渾源劉捴愛其才俊，以女妻之，遂傳其賦學，登天德三年詞賦進士第。

translations.literal: Liu Cui of Hunyuan loved his talent and gave him his daughter in marriage; he thereupon transmitted his fu studies, and Yuanjie passed the jinshi in rhapsody and fu in the third year of Tiande.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cui of Hunyuan admired his talent and gave him his daughter in marriage, transmitting his fu studies to him. Yuanjie passed the jinshi examination in rhapsody and fu in the third year of Tiande.

sentences.zh: 雅尚氣節，不能隨時俯仰，故仕不顯。

translations.literal: He esteemed integrity and could not bow and scrape with the times, so his office was not prominent.
translations.idiomatic: He prized integrity and could not bow and scrape with the times, and therefore never rose to prominence in office.

sentences.zh: 及遷密州觀察判官，既罷，即逍遙鄉里，以詩酒自娛，號曰「遁齊」。

translations.literal: When he was transferred to administrative judge of the Mizhou observation commission and then dismissed, he at once wandered freely in his home district, amusing himself with poetry and wine, styling himself "Recluse of Qi."
translations.idiomatic: When he was transferred to administrative judge of the Mizhou observation commission and then dismissed, he retired to his home district, amusing himself with poetry and wine, and styled himself "Recluse of Qi."

sentences.zh: 年五十餘卒。

translations.literal: He died in his fifties.
translations.idiomatic: He died in his fifties.

sentences.zh: 有詩集行於世。

translations.literal: He had a poetry collection circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry collection circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 弟元德，亦第進士。

translations.literal: His younger brother Yuande also passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Yuande also passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 有能名于時，終南京路提刑使。

translations.literal: He had a reputation for ability in his time and ended as transport commissioner of the Nanjing Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He enjoyed a reputation for ability in his time and ended his career as transport commissioner of the Nanjing Circuit.

sentences.zh: 孫國綱

translations.literal: Sun Guogang
translations.idiomatic: Sun Guogang

sentences.zh: 孫國綱，字正之。

translations.literal: Sun Guogang, styled Zhengzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Guogang, whose style name was Zhengzhi.

sentences.zh: 業儒術，尤長吏事。

translations.literal: He pursued Confucian learning and was especially skilled in administrative affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued Confucian learning and was especially skilled in administrative affairs.

sentences.zh: 為人端重樂易，或有忤者，略不與校，亦未嘗形於怒色。

translations.literal: In person he was dignified and easygoing; when someone crossed him he scarcely contended and never showed anger on his face.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was dignified and easygoing; when someone crossed him he scarcely argued back and never showed anger on his face.

sentences.zh: 大安三年，試補尚書吏部掾，未幾，轉御史台令史。

translations.literal: In the third year of Da'an he tested as a clerk in the Department of State Affairs and soon transferred to secretary of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Da'an he qualified as a clerk in the Department of State Affairs and soon transferred to secretary of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 宣宗聞其材幹，興定三年特召為近侍，奉職承應，甚見寵遇，勒留凡三考，出為同知申州事。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong heard of his ability; in the third year of Xingding he was specially summoned as a close attendant, serving as duty attendant, and was greatly favored. He was detained through three evaluations, then left office as Vice Commissioner of Shen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong heard of his ability and in the third year of Xingding specially summoned him as a close attendant, where he served with great favor. He was retained through three evaluations, then left to serve as Vice Commissioner of Shen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 無何，召為筆硯直長，擢監察御史，秩滿，敕留再任，蓋知其材器故也。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned as Director of Writing Implements, promoted to Investigating Censor, and when his term ended was ordered to remain for another term — because they knew his talent.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was summoned as Director of Writing Implements and promoted to Investigating Censor. When his term ended he was ordered to serve another term, for the court knew his talent.

sentences.zh: 開興元年，關陝完顏總帥屯河中府，與大元軍戰敗績，哀宗遣國綱乘上廄馬，徑詣河中問敗軍之由，還至中途，值大兵見殺，時年四十四。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaixing, the Wanyan commander-in-chief of Guan and Shaan stationed at Hezhong suffered defeat against the Great Yuan army. Emperor Aizong sent Guogang on an imperial stable horse straight to Hezhong to inquire into the defeat; on the return journey midway he encountered the great army and was killed, aged forty-four.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kaixing the Wanyan commander-in-chief of Guan and Shaan, stationed at Hezhong, was defeated by the Great Yuan army. Emperor Aizong sent Guogang on an imperial stable horse straight to Hezhong to investigate the defeat. On the return journey he encountered the enemy army midway and was killed at the age of forty-four.

sentences.zh: 麻九疇

translations.literal: Ma Jiuchou
translations.idiomatic: Ma Jiuchou

sentences.zh: 麻九疇，字知幾，易州人。

translations.literal: Ma Jiuchou, styled Zhiji, was a man of Yi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Jiuchou, whose style name was Zhiji, came from Yi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 三歲識字。

translations.literal: At three he knew characters.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of three he could recognize written characters.

sentences.zh: 七歲能草書，作大字有及數尺者，一時目為神童。

translations.literal: At seven he could write cursive script; large characters he wrote reached several feet — for a time he was regarded as a divine child.
translations.idiomatic: At seven he could write cursive script, and the large characters he produced reached several feet in size — for a time he was regarded as a divine child.

sentences.zh: 章宗召見，問：「汝入宮殿中，亦懼怯否？

translations.literal: Emperor Zhangzong summoned him and asked: "If you enter the palace halls, are you also afraid?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhangzong summoned him and asked, "If you enter the palace halls, are you also afraid?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「君臣，父子也。

translations.literal: He replied: "Sovereign and minister are like father and son."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Sovereign and minister are like father and son."

sentences.zh: 子甯懼父耶？

translations.literal: Would a son fear his father?"
translations.idiomatic: Would a son fear his father?"

sentences.zh: 」上大奇之。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly marveled at this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly impressed.

sentences.zh: 弱冠入太學，有文名。

translations.literal: In his weak-crown years he entered the Imperial Academy and gained a literary name.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he entered the Imperial Academy and gained a literary reputation.

sentences.zh: 南渡後，寓居郾、蔡間，入遂平西山，始以古學自力。

translations.literal: After the southern crossing he lived between Yan and Cai, entered the western hills of Suiping, and began to strengthen himself through ancient learning.
translations.idiomatic: After the court crossed south he lived between Yan and Cai, then entered the western hills of Suiping and began to strengthen himself through ancient learning.

sentences.zh: 博通《五經》，于《易》、《春秋》為尤長。

translations.literal: He mastered the Five Classics broadly and was especially accomplished in the Changes and the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered the Five Classics broadly and was especially accomplished in the Changes and the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 興定末，試開封府，詞賦第二，經義第一。

translations.literal: At the end of Xingding he tested at the Kaifeng prefectural office — second in rhapsody and fu, first in classical exegesis.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Xingding era he tested at the Kaifeng prefectural office, placing second in rhapsody and fu and first in classical exegesis.

sentences.zh: 再試南省，複然。

translations.literal: Testing again at the southern capital, the result was the same.
translations.idiomatic: When he tested again at the southern capital, the result was the same.

sentences.zh: 聲譽大振，雖婦人小兒皆知其名。

translations.literal: His fame shook greatly; even women and children knew his name.
translations.idiomatic: His fame spread far and wide; even women and children knew his name.

sentences.zh: 及廷試，以誤絀，士論惜之。

translations.literal: At the palace examination he erred in formatting; scholarly opinion regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: At the palace examination he made a formatting error, to the regret of scholarly opinion.

sentences.zh: 已而隱居不為科舉計。

translations.literal: Thereafter he lived in seclusion and made no plans for the examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he lived in seclusion and made no further plans for the examinations.

sentences.zh: 正大初，門人王說、王采苓俱中第，上以其年幼，怪而問之。

translations.literal: In early Zhengda his disciples Wang Yue and Wang Cailing both passed; the emperor, seeing their youth, wondered and inquired.
translations.idiomatic: In early Zhengda his disciples Wang Yue and Wang Cailing both passed the examinations. Seeing how young they were, the emperor wondered and inquired.

sentences.zh: 乃知嘗師九疇。

translations.literal: Only then was it learned that they had studied under Jiuchou.
translations.idiomatic: Only then was it learned that they had studied under Jiuchou.

sentences.zh: 平章政事侯摯、翰林學士趙秉文連章薦之，特賜盧亞榜進士第。

translations.literal: Grand Councilor Hou Zhi and Hanlin Academician Zhao Bingwen submitted successive memorials recommending him; he was specially granted the jinshi on the Lu Ya list.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councilor Hou Zhi and Hanlin Academician Zhao Bingwen submitted successive memorials recommending him, and he was specially granted the jinshi on the Lu Ya list.

sentences.zh: 以病，未拜官告歸。

translations.literal: Because of illness he did not receive appointment and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Because of illness he did not receive appointment and returned home.

sentences.zh: 再授太常寺太祝，權博士，俄遷應奉翰林文字。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Grand Sacrificer of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, acting as erudite, and soon promoted to Attendant Scribe of the Hanlin.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed Grand Sacrificer of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices with acting rank as erudite, and soon promoted to Attendant Scribe of the Hanlin.

sentences.zh: 九疇性資野逸，高蹇自便，與人交，一語不相入則逕去不返顧。

translations.literal: Jiuchou's nature was wild and free, lofty and self-willed; in dealing with people, if a single remark did not agree he would leave at once and never look back.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuchou's nature was wild and free, lofty and self-willed. In dealing with people, if a single remark failed to agree with him he would leave at once and never look back.

sentences.zh: 自度終不能與世合，頃之，複謝病去。

translations.literal: Judging that he could never harmonize with the world, before long he again pleaded illness and left.
translations.idiomatic: Judging that he could never harmonize with the world, before long he again pleaded illness and left office.

sentences.zh: 居郾城，天興元年，大元兵入河南，挈家走確山，為兵士所得，驅至廣平，病死，年五十。

translations.literal: Living at Yancheng, in the first year of Tianxing the Great Yuan army entered Henan; he took his family and fled to Queshan, was seized by soldiers, driven to Guangping, and died of illness, aged fifty.
translations.idiomatic: Living at Yancheng, in the first year of Tianxing the Great Yuan army entered Henan. He took his family and fled to Queshan, was seized by soldiers, driven to Guangping, and died of illness at the age of fifty.

sentences.zh: 九疇初因經義學《易》，後喜邵堯夫《皇極書》，因學算數，又喜卜筮、射覆之術。
