translations.literal: Jiuchou first studied the Changes through classical exegesis, later delighted in Shao Yongs Huangji writings and therefore studied mathematics, and also delighted in divination and guessing games.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuchou first studied the Changes through classical exegesis, later delighted in Shao Yong's Huangji writings and studied mathematics, and also delighted in divination and guessing games.

sentences.zh: 晚更喜醫，與名醫張子和遊，盡傳其學，且為潤色其所著書。

translations.literal: In his later years he came to delight in medicine, associated with the famous physician Zhang Zihe, fully transmitted his learning, and even polished the books he wrote.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he turned to medicine, associated with the famous physician Zhang Zihe, fully mastered his learning, and even polished the books Zhang wrote.

sentences.zh: 為文精密奇健，詩尤工致。

translations.literal: In prose he was precise, dense, and forceful; in poetry especially refined.
translations.idiomatic: In prose he was precise, dense, and forceful; in poetry especially refined.

sentences.zh: 後以避謗忌，持戒不作。

translations.literal: Later, to avoid slander and jealousy, he took a vow and ceased composing.
translations.idiomatic: Later, to avoid slander and jealousy, he took a vow and ceased composing.

sentences.zh: 明昌以來，稱神童者五人，太原常添壽四歲能作詩，劉滋、劉微、張漢臣後皆無稱，獨知幾能自樹立，耆舊如趙秉文，以征君目之而不名。

translations.literal: Since Mingchang five were called divine children; Taiyuan's Chang Tianshou could compose poetry at four — Liu Zi, Liu Wei, and Zhang Hanchen later had no reputation, while Zhiji alone could stand on his own. Elders such as Zhao Bingwen regarded him as a recluse by title and did not name him.
translations.idiomatic: Since Mingchang five were called divine children; Chang Tianshou of Taiyuan could compose poetry at four — Liu Zi, Liu Wei, and Zhang Hanchen later won no reputation, while Zhiji alone could stand on his own. Elders such as Zhao Bingwen regarded him as a recluse by title and did not record his name.

sentences.zh: 李汾，字長源，太原平晉人。

translations.literal: Li Fen, styled Changyuan, was a man of Pingjin in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fen, whose style name was Changyuan, came from Pingjin in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 為人尚氣，跌宕不羈。

translations.literal: By nature he prized spirit and was unrestrained and unbridled.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he prized spirit and was unrestrained and unbridled.

sentences.zh: 性褊躁，觸之輒怒，以是多為人所惡。

translations.literal: His temperament was narrow and quick; touch him and he grew angry — for this many hated him.
translations.idiomatic: His temperament was narrow and quick; touch him and he grew angry, and for this many people disliked him.

sentences.zh: 喜讀史。

translations.literal: He delighted in reading history.
translations.idiomatic: He delighted in reading history.

sentences.zh: 工詩，雄健有法。

translations.literal: Skilled in poetry, bold and regulated in method.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled in poetry, writing in a bold and disciplined manner.

sentences.zh: 避亂入關，京兆尹子容愛其材，招致門下。

translations.literal: Fleeing disorder he entered the passes; the metropolitan magistrate Zirong loved his talent and received him in his household.
translations.idiomatic: Fleeing the disorders he entered the passes. The metropolitan magistrate Zirong admired his talent and received him into his household.

sentences.zh: 留二年去，之涇州，竭左丞張行信，一見即以上客禮之。

translations.literal: After two years he left and went to Jing Prefecture, exhausting himself to visit Left Councilor Zhang Xingxin, who at first sight treated him with the courtesy due a distinguished guest.
translations.idiomatic: After two years he left and went to Jing Prefecture, where he sought out Left Councilor Zhang Xingxin, who at first sight treated him with the courtesy due a distinguished guest.

sentences.zh: 元光間，游大樑，舉進士不中，用薦為史館書寫。

translations.literal: In the Yuanguang era he traveled to Daliang, failed the jinshi examination, and on recommendation was made a copyist of the History Institute.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanguang era he traveled to Daliang, failed the jinshi examination, and on recommendation was appointed copyist of the History Institute.

sentences.zh: 書寫，特抄書小史耳，凡編修官得日錄，纂述即定，以稿授書寫，書寫錄潔本呈翰長。

translations.literal: A copyist is merely a minor clerk who copies books; whenever a compiler obtains the daily record and the compilation is settled, the draft is handed to the copyist, who records a fair copy and presents it to the chief of the Hanlin.
translations.idiomatic: A copyist is merely a minor clerk who copies books. Whenever a compiler obtained the daily record and the compilation was settled, the draft was handed to the copyist, who recorded a fair copy and presented it to the chief of the Hanlin.

sentences.zh: 汾既為之，殊不自聊。

translations.literal: Fen, having taken this post, was extremely ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Fen, having taken this post, was deeply ill at ease.

sentences.zh: 時趙秉文為學士，雷淵、李獻能皆在院，刊修之際，汾在旁正襟危坐，讀太史公、左丘明一篇，或數百言，音吐洪暢，旁若無人。

translations.literal: At the time Zhao Bingwen was academician; Lei Yuan and Li Xianneng were all in the academy. During revision Fen sat upright with grave deportment beside them, reading a piece by Grand Historian or Zuo Qiuming of several hundred words in a resonant, flowing voice as if no one were present.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zhao Bingwen was academician and Lei Yuan and Li Xianneng were all in the academy. During revision Fen sat upright beside them and read a passage from the Grand Historian or Zuo Qiuming of several hundred words in a resonant, flowing voice as if no one were present.

sentences.zh: 既畢，顧四坐漫為一語雲「看」。

translations.literal: When finished he glanced at the four seats and casually said one word: "Look."
translations.idiomatic: When he finished he glanced around the room and casually said, "Look."

sentences.zh: 秉筆諸人積不平，而雷、李尤切齒，乃以嫚罵官長訟於有司，然時論亦有不直雷、李者。

translations.literal: Those holding the brush were long resentful, and Lei and Li especially gnashed their teeth; they sued him before the authorities for insulting superiors, yet opinion of the time also held Lei and Li not entirely in the right.
translations.idiomatic: Those holding the brush had long resented him, and Lei and Li especially hated him. They sued him before the authorities for insulting superiors, yet opinion of the time also held that Lei and Li were not entirely in the right.

sentences.zh: 尋罷入關。

translations.literal: Soon he was dismissed and entered the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was dismissed and returned to the passes.

sentences.zh: 明年來京師，上書言時事，不合，去客唐、鄧間。

translations.literal: The next year he came to the capital and submitted a memorial on current affairs; it did not fit and he left to sojourn between Tang and Deng.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he came to the capital and submitted a memorial on current affairs. When it was rejected he left to sojourn between Tang and Deng.

sentences.zh: 恆山公武仙署行尚書省講議官。

translations.literal: Duke Wuxian of Hengshan appointed him discussion officer of the provisional Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Wuxian of Hengshan appointed him discussion officer of the provisional Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 既而仙與參知政事完顏思烈相異同，頗謀自安，懼汾言論，欲除之。

translations.literal: Soon Wuxian and Participating Councilor Wanyan Silie differed in views and plotted somewhat for their own security; fearing Fen's talk, they wished to eliminate him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Wuxian and Participating Councilor Wanyan Silie differed in their views and sought their own security. Fearing Fen's outspokenness, they wished to eliminate him.

sentences.zh: 汾覺，遁泌陽，仙令總帥王德追獲之，鎖養馬平，絕食而死，年未四十。

translations.literal: Fen perceived this and fled to Biyang; Wuxian ordered Commander Wang De to pursue and capture him, locked him at Yangmaping, and he died by starvation, not yet forty.
translations.idiomatic: Fen perceived this and fled to Biyang. Wuxian ordered Commander Wang De to pursue and capture him, locked him at Yangmaping, and he died by starvation before the age of forty.

sentences.zh: 汾平生詩甚多，不自收集，世所傳者十二三而已。

translations.literal: Fen in his lifetime had very many poems but did not collect them himself; what the world transmits is only twelve or thirteen tenths.
translations.idiomatic: Fen wrote a great many poems in his lifetime but did not collect them himself; only about twelve or thirteen tenths of them circulate in the world.

sentences.zh: 元德明

translations.literal: Yuan Deming
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Deming

sentences.zh: 元德明，系出拓拔魏，太原秀容人。

translations.literal: Yuan Deming traced his line to the Tuoba Wei and was a man of Xiurong in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Deming traced his line to the Tuoba Wei and came from Xiurong in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 自幼嗜讀書，口不言世俗鄙事，樂易無畦畛，布衣蔬食處之自若，家人不敢以生理累之。

translations.literal: From childhood he loved reading and never spoke of vulgar worldly matters. Easygoing without boundaries, he wore plain cloth and ate simple food as if it were natural; his family did not dare burden him with livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he loved reading and never spoke of vulgar worldly matters. Easygoing and without pretension, he wore plain cloth and ate simple food as if it were natural, and his family did not dare burden him with worldly livelihood.

sentences.zh: 累舉不第，放浪山水間，餘酒賦詩以自適。

translations.literal: He failed the examinations repeatedly and wandered freely among mountains and waters, spending his surplus on wine and composing poetry for his own pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: He failed the examinations repeatedly and wandered freely among mountains and waters, spending his surplus on wine and composing poetry for his own pleasure.

sentences.zh: 年四十八卒。

translations.literal: He died at forty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of forty-eight.

sentences.zh: 有《東岩集》三卷。

translations.literal: He had Eastern Cliff Collection in three juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left the Eastern Cliff Collection in three juan.

sentences.zh: 子好問，最知名。

translations.literal: His son Haowen was the most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: His son Haowen was the most renowned.

sentences.zh: 子 元好問

translations.literal: His son Yuan Haowen
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuan Haowen

sentences.zh: 好問字裕之。

translations.literal: Haowen was styled Yuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Haowen, whose style name was Yuzhi.

sentences.zh: 七歲能詩。

translations.literal: At seven he could compose poetry.
translations.idiomatic: He could compose poetry at the age of seven.

sentences.zh: 年十有四，從陵川郝晉卿學，不事舉業，淹貫經傳百家，六年而業成。

translations.literal: At fourteen he studied under Hao Jinqing of Lingchuan, did not pursue examination studies, and thoroughly mastered the classics and the hundred schools — in six years his learning was complete.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he studied under Hao Jinqing of Lingchuan without pursuing examination studies, and in six years he thoroughly mastered the classics and the hundred schools.

sentences.zh: 下太行，渡大河，為《箕山》、《琴台》等詩。

translations.literal: He descended the Taihang, crossed the great river, and composed poems such as "Mount Ji" and "Zither Terrace."
translations.idiomatic: He descended the Taihang, crossed the Yellow River, and composed poems such as "Mount Ji" and "Zither Terrace."

sentences.zh: 禮部趙秉文見之，以為近代無此作也。

translations.literal: Zhao Bingwen of the Ministry of Rites saw them and said that in recent times there had been nothing like this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Bingwen of the Ministry of Rites read them and declared that in recent times there had been nothing like them.

sentences.zh: 於是名震京師。

translations.literal: From this his name shook the capital.
translations.idiomatic: From this his name shook the capital.

sentences.zh: 中興定五年第，曆內鄉令。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhongxingding he passed the examinations and served successively as magistrate of Neixiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Zhongxingding he passed the examinations and served successively as magistrate of Neixiang.

sentences.zh: 正大中，為南陽令。

translations.literal: In the Zhengda era he was magistrate of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhengda era he served as magistrate of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 天興初，擢尚書省掾，頃之，除左司都事，轉行尚書省左司員外郎。

translations.literal: In early Tianxing he was promoted to clerk of the Department of State Affairs; before long he was made Director of the Left Department, then transferred to Vice Director of the Left Department of the Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In early Tianxing he was promoted to clerk of the Department of State Affairs; before long he was made Director of the Left Department, then transferred to Vice Director of the Left Department of the Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 金亡，不仕。

translations.literal: When Jin fell he did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin fell he did not take office under the new regime.

sentences.zh: 為文有繩尺，備眾體。

translations.literal: In writing he had standards and mastered every form.
translations.idiomatic: In writing he had clear standards and mastered every literary form.

sentences.zh: 其詩奇崛而絕雕劌，巧縟而謝綺麗。

translations.literal: His poetry was striking and lofty yet utterly without carving, ingenious and dense yet rejecting ornate elegance.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry was striking and lofty yet utterly without ornamental carving, ingenious and dense yet rejecting gaudy elegance.

sentences.zh: 五言高古沈鬱。

translations.literal: Five-character verse was lofty, ancient, and somber.
translations.idiomatic: His five-character verse was lofty, ancient, and somber.

sentences.zh: 七言樂府不用古題，特出新意。

translations.literal: Seven-character yuefu did not use ancient titles but specially brought forth new ideas.
translations.idiomatic: His seven-character yuefu did not use ancient titles but brought forth new ideas of his own.

sentences.zh: 歌謠慷慨，挾幽、并之氣。

translations.literal: Ballads were impassioned, carrying the spirit of You and Bing.
translations.idiomatic: His ballads were impassioned, carrying the spirit of You and Bing.

sentences.zh: 其長短句，揄揚新聲，以寫恩怨者又數百篇。

translations.literal: In song lyrics he set new tunes to express gratitude and resentment — several hundred more such pieces.
translations.idiomatic: In song lyrics he set new tunes to express gratitude and resentment in several hundred more pieces.

sentences.zh: 兵後，故老皆盡，好問蔚為一代宗工，四方碑板銘志，盡趨其門。

translations.literal: After the wars the old generation was all gone; Haowen towered as the master of an age, and steles, inscriptions, and epitaphs from the four directions all hurried to his door.
translations.idiomatic: After the wars the old generation was gone. Haowen stood as the master of an age, and steles, inscriptions, and epitaphs from every direction hurried to his door.

sentences.zh: 其所著文章詩若干卷、《杜詩學》一卷、《東坡詩雅》三卷、《錦禨》一卷、《詩文自警》十卷。

translations.literal: His writings included several juan of prose and poetry, Studies in Du Fu's Poetry in one juan, Poetic Standards of Su Dongpo in three juan, Brocade Admonitions in one juan, and Literary Self-Warnings in ten juan.
translations.idiomatic: His writings included several juan of prose and poetry, Studies in Du Fu's Poetry in one juan, Poetic Standards of Su Dongpo in three juan, Brocade Admonitions in one juan, and Literary Self-Warnings in ten juan.

sentences.zh: 晚年尤以著作自任，以金源氏有天下，典章法度幾及漢、唐，國亡史作，己所當任。

translations.literal: In his later years he especially charged himself with authorship, holding that since the Jin source family had possessed the realm and its institutions and laws nearly matched Han and Tang, when the state perished the history should be written — and this was his duty.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he especially charged himself with authorship, holding that since the Jin had possessed the realm and its institutions nearly matched Han and Tang, when the state perished the history must be written — and this was his duty.

sentences.zh: 時金國實錄在順天張萬戶家，乃言于張，願為撰述，既而為樂夔所沮而止。

translations.literal: At the time the Jin veritable records were in the household of Zhang the ten-thousand-bushel master of Shuntian; he spoke to Zhang and wished to compile them, but was stopped when Yue Kui obstructed it.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Jin veritable records were kept in the household of Zhang the ten-thousand-bushel master of Shuntian. He spoke to Zhang and offered to compile them, but Yue Kui obstructed the plan and it came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 好問曰：「不可令一代之跡泯而不傳。

translations.literal: Haowen said: "One must not let the traces of an age perish without transmission."
translations.idiomatic: Haowen said, "One must not let the traces of an age perish without being passed down."

sentences.zh: 」乃構亭於家，著述其上，因名曰「野史」。

translations.literal: He then built a pavilion at home and wrote upon it, naming it for this reason "Unofficial History."
translations.idiomatic: He then built a pavilion at his home and wrote upon it, naming it "Unofficial History" for that reason.

sentences.zh: 凡金源君臣遺言往行，采摭所聞，有所得輒以寸紙細字為記錄，至百余萬言。

translations.literal: As for the sayings and deeds of Jin sovereigns and ministers, he gathered what he heard; whenever he gained something he at once recorded it in fine script on a small sheet, reaching more than a million characters.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered whatever he heard of the words and deeds of Jin sovereigns and ministers, recording each discovery in fine script on a small sheet of paper until his notes ran to more than a million characters.

sentences.zh: 今所傳者有《中州集》及《壬辰雜編》若干卷。

translations.literal: What is transmitted today includes Central Plains Collection and Miscellaneous Records of the Renchen year in several juan.
translations.idiomatic: What circulates today includes the Central Plains Collection and Miscellaneous Records of the Renchen year in several juan.

sentences.zh: 年六十八卒。

translations.literal: He died aged sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 纂修《金史》，多本其所著雲。

translations.literal: In compiling the History of Jin, much was based on his writings.
translations.idiomatic: The compilers of the History of Jin drew heavily upon his writings.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：韓昉、吳激，楚材而晉用之，亦足為一代之文矣。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Han Fang and Wu Ji — Chu talent employed by Jin — were also sufficient as writers of an age.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: Han Fang and Wu Ji were Chu talents employed by the Jin, and they too were writers worthy of their age.

sentences.zh: 蔡珪、馬定國之該博，胡礪、楊伯仁之敏贍，鄭子聃、麻九疇之英俊，王郁、宋九嘉之邁往。

translations.literal: Cai Gui and Ma Dingguo's comprehensive learning; Hu Li and Yang Boren's quick abundance; Zheng Zidan and Ma Jiuchou's brilliance; Wang Yu and Song Jiujia's bold advance.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Gui and Ma Dingguo were comprehensively learned; Hu Li and Yang Boren were quick and prolific; Zheng Zidan and Ma Jiuchou were brilliant; Wang Yu and Song Jiujia were boldly forward-looking.

sentences.zh: 三李卓犖，純甫知道，汾任氣，獻能尤以純孝見稱。

translations.literal: The three Lis stood out: Chunfu knew the Way, Fen relied on spirit, and Xianneng was especially praised for pure filial devotion.
translations.idiomatic: The three Lis stood above the rest: Chunfu knew the Way, Fen relied on force of character, and Xianneng was especially praised for pure filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 王庭筠、党懷英、元好問自足知名異代。

translations.literal: Wang Tingyun, Dang Huaiying, and Yuan Haowen were sufficient in themselves to be famed in another age.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tingyun, Dang Huaiying, and Yuan Haowen were sufficient in themselves to win fame in any age.

sentences.zh: 王競、劉從益、王若虛之吏治，文不掩其所長。

translations.literal: Wang Jing, Liu Congyi, and Wang Ruoxu's governance in office — their writing does not obscure their strengths.
translations.idiomatic: In the governance of Wang Jing, Liu Congyi, and Wang Ruoxu, their literary fame does not obscure their strengths as officials.

sentences.zh: 蔡松年在文藝中，爵位之最重者，道金人言利，興黨獄，殺田玨，文不能掩其所短者歟？

translations.literal: Cai Songnian, among men of literary arts the heaviest in rank, preached Jin people's profit, raised factional prosecutions, and killed Tian Yu — can writing not cover his shortcomings?
translations.idiomatic: Cai Songnian held the highest rank among men of letters, preached profit for the Jin, raised factional prosecutions, and killed Tian Yu — can literary talent truly cover shortcomings such as these?

sentences.zh: 事繼母有至行，其死家無餘貲，有足取雲。

translations.literal: In serving his stepmother he had utmost conduct; at his death the family had no surplus funds — there is still something to be taken from this.
translations.idiomatic: In serving his stepmother he showed exemplary devotion, and at his death his family had no surplus wealth — in this there is still something admirable.
